deities: Goddess Ekanatheshwari (incarnation of Adi Parashakti; presiding family/kuladeva deity of the Nayakas of Chitradurga)
festivals: Okuli festival (rites at the granite stone in front of the temple - details unverified, verify)

history.dynasty: Nayakas of Chitradurga (Palegar Nayakas, 15th-18th century; the fort's temples were built/rebuilt in their era)
history.period: Nayaka period (15th-18th century - verify; fort temples expanded then)
history.summary: One of the 18 temples of the upper Chitradurga Fort and the presiding family deity (kuladeva) of the Nayakas of Chitradurga. Her footprints are sculpted into a block of stone at the fort's entrance. The temple stands just past the seventh gateway, with a tall deepasthamba (lamp tower, lit at the top) and an uyyala kambha (swing pillar) in front; a granite stone built in front of the temple is used for the Okuli festival. Historically and emotionally she remains an inspiration to the people of Chitradurga.

name: Ekanatheshwari Temple
town: Inside Chitradurga Fort, Chitradurga (CSV town 'Chitradurga' correct)
town_description: Inside the upper fort of Chitradurga (Elusuttina Kote), past the seventh gateway. Shares the fort's ~1500-acre rocky-hill setting with the other 17 upper-fort temples, the Onake Obavva Kindi, the Kallina Kote palace and the famous rainwater-harvesting tanks.

travel.airport: Hubli - about 186 km; Bengaluru (Kempegowda International) - about 197 km (both domestic/international options per travel guides).
travel.railway: Chitradurga railway station - buses and taxis available to the fort.
travel.road: Chitradurga city lies on NH-4/NH-48, ~200 km from Bengaluru (3-4 hrs by KSRTC bus incl. Airavat coaches); autos/taxis from Chitradurga bus stand to the fort.

visitor_information.opening_hours: Fort open 10:00 AM-5:30 PM daily (verify); entry fee reported INR 20 (e-ticket)/25 (cash) for Indian/SAARC/BIMSTEC visitors and INR 250/300 for other foreign nationals, free for children below 15 (verify); no separate entry fee for the temple.
